key_insight: The paper shows that robust learning under Wasserstein DRO can be made more effective by designing adversarial examples as globally optimal transport maps that satisfy cyclical monotonicity, rather than independent per-sample perturbations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to build more reliable models for safety-critical AI systems by improving robustness to distribution shift while reducing wasted adversarial effort.
method: Reformulate the adversary as a transport-map optimization problem under a Wasserstein penalty.
Use multi-start particle ascent with reassignment to enforce cyclical monotonicity across samples.
Parameterize adversarial maps with gradients of input-convex neural networks to guarantee monotone transport by design.
evidence_signal: The methods were evaluated on robust regression, image classification, and robust control, where they consistently outperformed standard adversarial training and strong baselines under distribution shift.
watch_item: The proposed methods add optimization and model-design complexity, so their training stability and computational cost may be a concern in large-scale deployments.
paper_title: Brenier Meets Adversarial Training: Optimal Transport Geometry for Robust Learning
